# The implementer leaves a forbidden command, and every review approves with the gate green.
# The first fix hits too, so the scoped loop goes on: a hit in any lane run forces another fix. The clean second fix ends it.
exec beehest run 7 --workflow flow/workflow.star
stdout 'item 7 finished'

exec beehest status
stdout '^item-7-r1\tdone\tgate pass at [0-9a-f]+\treview 3/24\t'

# Both fixes belong to candidate 1, so both are round 1. Two scoped reviews and the full review.
grep -count=1 '^plan ' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^implement ' calls.log
grep -count=3 '^review ' calls.log
grep -count=2 '^fix 1 ' calls.log
! grep '^fix 2 ' calls.log

# The scoped review after the first fix sees its hit. The scoped review after the clean second fix and the full review see none.
grep -count=1 '^bulk-staging: git add -A$' seen.log

# Both fixes get the hit of the run before them as the first line of their findings.
grep -count=2 '^fix: bulk-staging: git add -A$' found.log
! grep '^settle ' calls.log

cmp events.log expected-events.log

-- verdicts --
approve
approve
approve
-- fixhits --
hit
clean
-- expected-events.log --
claim 7
release 7
